chunks: And a group informed me from several of our companions from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from al-Husayn ibn Abdullah from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Rabat from Ibn Azaynah from Zurarah, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: The twelve Imams from the family of Muhammad are all Muhaddathun (those endowed with divine speech/knowledge), from the descendants of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the descendants of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). Thus, the Messenger of Allah and Ali are their fathers.
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve Imams and what is their spiritual status according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* reinforces the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility) by classifying the Twelve Imams as *Muhaddathun*, a status distinct from mere prophets, indicating they receive divine inspiration. It highlights their genealogical purity by tracing their lineage directly through the dual progenitors, Prophet Muhammad and Ali ibn Abi Talib, thereby establishing their unique authority in Shia theology. This hadith serves as a foundational proof for the fixed number of Imams and their continuous line of divine guidance within the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 112 - Informed me a group of scholar from Muhammad bin Yaqub from Ali Ashari from Husain bin Abdullah from Hasan from Musa Khashshab from Hasan bin Sama-a from Ali bin Hasan bin Rabat from Ibn Uzniyya from Zurarah that he said:

I heard Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) say: Twelve Imams from Aale Muhammad (a.s) were all Muhaddath and they were from the descendants of the Messenger of Allah (s) and Ali Ibn Abi Talib (a.s). Thus the Messenger of Allah (s) and Imam Ali (a.s) are their fathers.
